title: Man dies in Edmonton police custody; nabbed at City Centre Mall
article: A 25-year-old man died after being arrested by city police at City Centre Mall Wednesday night.
City police arrested the man after a 10 p.m. trespassing call at a mall in the downtown core.
The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) -- which is now leading the investigation into the death -- said in a statement that police arrived for a "disturbance" complaint.
"They found an agitated 25-year-old man who had been arrested for trespassing and was in the custody of City Centre Mall Security," says the ASIRT statement.

"At approximately 10:30 p.m., police took custody of the man and transported him to Edmonton Police Service headquarters. As they entered headquarters, the man went into medical distress and became unresponsive. Emergency Medical Services was immediately called and then arrived to provide emergency medical care. The man was taken by ambulance to hospital where, shortly before 4 a.m., he was declared deceased."
ASIRT was directed by the Director of Law Enforcement to investigate the circumstances of the medical distress and subsequent death of the man.
This is the second death in city police custody since November, when a man with a rare genetic disorder died in a cop van after being arrested.

In that case, police got a call from a medical clinic near 122 Avenue and 97 Street saying a man was acting aggressively toward staff. When they arrived, staff identified Trevor Proudman as the man in question.

Police spoke to the man and placed him in handcuffs before putting him into the paddy wagon. Officers then spent the next 10 to 15 minutes interviewing staff at the site. When officers returned to the van, Proudman was in medical distress. Emergency responders arrived and took Proudman to hospital. The next morning, Proudman was pronounced dead.

As no physical altercation took place, the Director of Law Enforcement has ruled that the city police service had the choice whether to investigate further. Police were reviewing the incident in order to determine best practices. In that case, ASIRT offered to review the city police findings, an offer the force accepted.

ASIRT's mandate is to effectively, independently, and objectively investigate incidents involving Alberta's police that have resulted in serious injury or death to any person, as well as serious or sensitive allegations of police misconduct.
Results of the investigation into the November case have not yet been released.
